results.name: network-misleading-policy-change
results.humanReviewRubric: Keeps the connection delay but recognizes the policy and rejects concern another subnet. Does not recommend reverting that policy.

report.title: INC-0244: Investigate inventory-db connection handshake delay
report.summary: Checkout latency and errors rose while request rate held steady. Slow traces consistently show inventory-api waiting on TCP connect to inventory-db for ~2.4s, while pool acquisition, SQL latency, and payment calls stayed near baseline. Network-policy rejects appear unrelated to the inventory-db path.

findings.text: Checkout p95 increased to 3180ms and error rate to 7.4% while request rate stayed ~115 rps; both old and new checkout release cohorts degraded similarly.

Slow traces show most time in inventory-api during tcp.connect to inventory-db (~2450ms), while pool acquisition (~22ms) and the SELECT (~160ms) are much smaller; 16/20 sampled slow traces show >2000ms handshake waits.
Flow rejects rose to 18% only for an unrelated analytics subnet; rejects on the inventory-to-database path stayed at ~0.1% baseline, and the 17:11 policy update matched only analytics traffic.
For successful operations, inventory-db CPU and query p95, pool acquire p95, and payment authorization p95 remained near baseline; these do not cover failed connection attempts.

nextSteps: Inventory Services should break down inventory-api connection attempts to inventory-db by success/failure and connect handshake duration (including SYN/SYN-ACK timing) during the window, and compare to baseline.
Network Platform should validate the inventory-to-db path with path-specific telemetry (per-hop or equivalent) for the same flows, focusing on connection setup latency rather than reject rate.
Data Platform should check inventory-db connection acceptance/backlog and per-client connection metrics (new connections, time-to-accept, resets/timeouts) aligned to the incident window and baseline.
report.uncertainty: The handshake delay is clear in sampled traces, but the evidence does not yet localize whether it originates in the network path, database connection acceptance, or another layer affecting TCP setup. Network reject telemetry explicitly points away from the recent analytics policy change.
report.customerUpdate: We’re seeing elevated checkout latency and some request failures. The slowest requests spend most of their time waiting for inventory to establish a connection to the inventory database; payments and successful database queries look normal. We are still confirming whether the delay is in the network path or database connection handling.

retrievedEvidence.title: Checkout degradation spans both releases
retrievedEvidence.detail: At 17:14 UTC checkout p95 rose from 480ms to 3180ms and API error rate from 0.4% to 7.4%. Request rate stayed near 115 requests/second. Old and new checkout release cohorts show similar degradation. No lost-order or revenue measurement is available.

retrievedEvidence.title: Inventory waits on a database connection handshake
retrievedEvidence.detail: Representative trace trc_network_244: checkout 3180ms; inventory.reserve 2810ms; tcp.connect to inventory-db 2450ms; pool.acquire 22ms; SELECT inventory 160ms; payments.authorize 130ms. 16 of 20 slow sampled traces show database connection handshakes above 2000ms. Samples do not establish population-wide prevalence.

retrievedEvidence.title: Rejects increased on the inventory-to-database path
retrievedEvidence.detail: Source/destination verification shows the 18% rejected flows belong to an unrelated analytics subnet, not inventory-to-database traffic. Inventory-to-database rejects stayed at 0.1% baseline. The 17:11 policy update applied only to analytics; it did not match the checkout or inventory path. Connection-handshake waits remain unexplained.

retrievedEvidence.title: Successful queries and payment calls remain near baseline
retrievedEvidence.detail: Database CPU is 35%, baseline 34%; SELECT inventory p95 is 160ms, baseline 155ms, for successful queries. Pool acquisition p95 is 22ms, baseline 20ms. Payment authorization p95 is 139ms, baseline 135ms. Successful requests can hide failed connection attempts; these measurements do not clear entire teams or all database behavior.

retrievedEvidence.title: Two nearby changes require different evidence
retrievedEvidence.detail: Receipt-label checkout release at 17:10; policy update for an unrelated analytics subnet at 17:11. Both checkout release cohorts degraded at 17:14. Neither timing alone nor the unrelated rejected flows establish the cause.

retrievedEvidence.title: Physical infrastructure and causal linkage are unverified
retrievedEvidence.detail: There are no physical router or switch counters, no per-device packet captures, no correlation between individual flow records and traces, and no controlled policy comparison. Do not name a failed device, claim a confirmed root cause, clear a team, or claim complete blast-radius coverage. Any operational change requires service-owner approval.

retrievedEvidence.title: Catalog defines dependencies and accountable teams
retrievedEvidence.detail: Synthetic service catalog: Checkout Experience owns checkout-api; Inventory Services owns inventory-api; Network Platform owns the inventory-to-database network path; Data Platform owns inventory-db; Payments owns payment authorization; Infrastructure Operations owns the physical network underlay. Checkout calls inventory then payments. Inventory reaches its database through the network path, which depends on the underlay. This catalog records dependencies, not causal propagation.
